name: Western Australia

gate.regulator_fallback: WA Department of Health Environmental Health Directorate
gate.mechanism: Register or notify with local government before operating. Food prepared in a residential home intended for sale requires Registration. Some Food Regulations 2009 exempt activities notify instead of register.
gate.fee_notes: Local government sets fees. Department of Health prescribed fees (for DoH-regulated sites only): notification $84, registration $255 under Food Regulations 2009.

scope.commodity_scheme_regulator: Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) / agric.wa.gov.au

channels.render_reason: 6 of 8 not_published, table suppressed per spec 7.12
channels.notes: Fundraising exemption from registration for non-PHF charitable food cooked for immediate consumption still requires notification.

labelling.basis: Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code, Standard 1.2.1
required_elements: Supplier name and street address in Australia or New Zealand
Warning and advisory statements, and allergen declaration
labelling.allergen_rule: Allergen declaration required as a Code label element

training.fss_trigger: Standard 3.2.2A Category 1 or 2: unpackaged, potentially hazardous food that is ready to eat (processing it, or selling it without making it).

food_safety_management.standard_322a_trigger: Applies to Category 1 and Category 2 food service, catering and retail businesses handling unpackaged, potentially hazardous ready-to-eat food.

unique.quirk_paragraph: DRAFT: Western Australia treats home-prepared food for sale as Registration with local government Environmental Health, with a separate notify path for regulated exemptions. Escalation needed for human polish of the register-versus-notify fork and the charitable fundraising carve-out.
unique.common_mistake: Assuming a low-risk home bake sale can skip contact with council because it feels informal.
unique.what_does_not_apply: Home kitchen use is framed for low-risk activity under Standard 3.2.3; DoH policy limits construction exemptions to low risk. Confirm product risk with your local EHO.

information_gain: Home food for sale requires Registration under the WA home-based table, not a soft informal notify-only path
Unregistered business maximum penalties published: A$10,000 individual and A$50,000 body corporate
Council fees are local; DoH prescribed fees apply only to DoH-regulated sites (notification A$84, registration A$255)
Charitable fundraising can be exempt from registration for non-PHF food cooked for immediate consumption, but must still notify
